summary: The bill requires U.S. Customs and Border Protection to automatically refund within 90 days all tariffs collected on imports since January 1, 2025, under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act by liquidating or reliquidating entries and paying importers without requiring any applications or protests.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates that CBP issue refunds of all IEEPA tariffs collected since January 1, 2025. These refunds constitute direct federal outlays to importers. While the amounts are not newly appropriated spending, the legislation compels the government to disburse funds it had already collected, producing a net expansionary effect on federal spending.
Tariffs are a form of tax. By requiring automatic, retroactive refunds of IEEPA tariffs, the bill effectively lowers the tax burden on importers and businesses that paid those duties.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare delivery, insurance, public programs, or market-based reforms.
No provisions address firearms, background checks, or gun rights.
Although the refunds are administered by CBP, the legislation addresses only tariff refunds and does not alter immigration enforcement, visa policy, or border security measures.
No provisions relate to reproductive health services or abortion access.
The bill does not authorize, modify, or affect military or defense appropriations.
No environmental regulations, energy policy, or climate provisions are present.
The legislation does not change eligibility, funding, or administration of welfare, SNAP, Medicaid, or other safety-net programs.
No education funding, school-choice, or federal education policy provisions appear in the bill.
The bill contains nothing related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance regulation.
No sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform measures are included.

The core purpose of the bill is to refund tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. By reversing these duties, the legislation moves policy away from protectionist or emergency tariff measures and toward freer trade.
Refunding collected tariff revenue reduces federal receipts and widens the deficit. This runs counter to prioritizing debt reduction.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
The bill does not authorize, reduce, or otherwise affect foreign assistance programs.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign-finance provisions are present.
The legislation does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or digital platforms.
No labor, union, or worker-protection measures are included.
The bill contains no religious-exemption or civil-rights provisions.
